gaps.sentence: ___ books you left on my desk were really useful.
gaps.explanation: 'The books you left…' — the clause identifies which books.

gaps.sentence: His mother went to ___ prison to visit him.
gaps.explanation: Visitors go to the building: 'went to the prison'.

gaps.sentence: We visited ___ Louvre on our last morning in Paris.
gaps.explanation: Most famous buildings and monuments take 'the': the Louvre, the Eiffel Tower.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ best film of the decade by common consent.
We had ___ awful weather on the crossing.
gaps.explanation: 'Weather' is uncountable — 'had awful weather', no article.

gaps.sentence: She spent three weeks in ___ hospital after the accident.
gaps.explanation: British English: be in hospital (as a patient) takes no article; the building is the hospital.

gaps.sentence: The car crashed into a wall at ___ speed of 90 km/h.
gaps.explanation: 'At a speed of…' — 'a' is part of this fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: His wife goes to ___ prison every Sunday to visit him.
gaps.explanation: Here 'the prison' is the building she visits, not the institution of imprisonment.
